thread:
Alex: quick datapoint from yesterday's perf run on rtx-p3 (80B workloads) — seeing OOMs during long chat sessions when KV churn hits ~45%
Marie: ouch. is this during steady state or right after a burst of small requests?
Alex: steady state. pattern: many short messages that create lots of short-lived KV segments. allocator fragmentation + compaction cost skyrockets.
Devon: can you paste the top-line profile? kernel select + mem ops?
Alex: pasted below from perf agent:
```
hotspot: block_manager::compact_blocks 37% CPU
hotspot: allocator::malloc 18% CPU
hotspot: kernel_selector::choose 9% CPU
kv_cache: eviction_scan 11% CPU
```
Marie: interesting that compact_blocks is the biggest. suggests we're paying heavy compaction tax not just fragmentation.
Sandeep: what are current block_size and reuse_policy?
Alex: block_size=32KB, reuse_policy=LRU with eager compaction when free_ratio < 0.22, and we run a background compactor every 2s.
Lucy: hypothesis: eager compaction thrashes when churn creates many tiny freed ranges -> constant mem moves. Could try increasing free_ratio threshold or batch compaction windows.
Devon: another lever: dynamic block splitting. Instead of compacting whole block, split hot sub-blocks into smaller segments to allow reuse and avoid moving cold pages. Reduces copy cost but increases metadata.
Marie: agree. Also consider switching allocator to slab arenas for small allocations (<2KB). That reduces meta-churn for short-lived KV entries.
Sandeep: any regression tied to kernel selection? maybe kernel switch overhead interacts badly with fragmentation.
Alex: yes, we saw a 6% tail latency bump when kernel_selector moved between fast-gemm and fallback for mid-length seqs. The extra memcpy/reshape between kernels exacerbates pressure on workspace allocator.
Devon: can we try two quick experiments: 1) double compaction window to 4s and raise free_ratio to 0.30; 2) enable slab arena for small KV entries and enable sub-block split for blocks with >60% small frees.
Lucy: I'll run (1) on canary and capture perf counters: compaction time, memcpy bandwidth, allocator stalls.
Marie: I'll prepare (2) with a feature-flagged allocator path. Need to watch metadata overhead (we have limited CPU for meta ops).
ops-bot: deployment request queued: canary-eng-runtime-2026-03-18 by Lucy.
Alex: thanks — when (1) runs, look at 'compact_blocks' cpu time and number of compaction passes per minute. If compaction time drops and OOMs stop, that's good. If memcpy bandwidth drops and kernel infra tail improves, we win.
Lucy: noting to capture these metrics: compact_pass_count, avg_compact_ms, memcpy_gb_s, kv_eviction_count, allocator_frag_ratio, kernel_switch_rate.
Sandeep: one more thought — add a cheap probabilistic eviction sampler to avoid scanning whole block for eviction candidates. That reduces eviction_scan cost.
Devon: good idea. sampler can run on allocation path and tag blocks for background compaction only when sampled hot. Cheap and low-risk.
Marie: we'll split tasks: Lucy runs config (1) tomorrow morning, I'll prototype slab allocator and sub-block split feature-flag this week. Devon/Sandeep to implement sampler. Alex to validate with long chat workload.
Alex: timeline acked. goal: eliminate OOMs for 12k+ token sessions and drop compact_blocks CPU by 50%.
Lucy: queued canary, will post results in this thread within 4h. :thumbsup:
Marie: thanks all. small reminder to annotate perf traces with kernel selection events so we can correlate memory ops to kernel swaps.
Alex: good call. adding trace hook now.
